findings.head: pr:health | HIGH | "that cap, not the premium, is the number your cash reserves should be able to cover"
findings.text:
Why: for a low-income reader, an out-of-pocket maximum of several thousand dollars is out of reach, so the advice reads as a standard they will fail. It leaves out three protections: lower out-of-pocket limits on silver plans for lower incomes, nonprofit hospitals' financial assistance, and Medicaid. "Most common route... to unpayable debt" is also a strong claim that CL525 (the out-of-pocket-max figure) may not support, and much medical debt falls on insured people.
Fix: "If that's out of reach, a silver plan with cost-sharing reductions can lower the cap, and nonprofit hospitals must offer financial assistance; ask before paying any big bill." Source the "most common route" claim or soften it to "a common route".

findings.head: pr:disability | MED | "disability is more likely than early death"
findings.text:
Why: this framing usually comes from insurer-funded groups, so it needs a named source. The block also assumes group LTD, which many low-wage and gig workers don't have, and it ignores SSDI and state disability programs.
Fix: name the source. Add: "Many workers have no group coverage. Social Security disability exists but is strict and slow, and some states run short-term disability or paid-leave programs."

findings.head: pr:auto | MED | "Liability well above the state minimum... umbrella carriers usually require higher underlying limits"
findings.text:
Why: the umbrella sentence nudges toward an upsell that most readers don't need. Uninsured motorist coverage, which protects the reader themselves, is left out.
Fix: replace the umbrella sentence with "Uninsured/underinsured motorist coverage pays you when the other driver can't, and is often the better use of a tight budget."

findings.head: pr:umbrella | MED | "roughly match coverage to net worth" / "inexpensive per dollar"
findings.text:
Why: this is industry framing, and net worth is the wrong measure. Retirement plans and some home equity are often protected from lawsuits, and a renter with modest savings rarely needs this.
Fix: "Most renters and households with modest savings don't need one. The question is what a lawsuit could actually reach, which usually excludes employer retirement plans."

findings.head: pr:emergency-fund vs pr:health — MED (internal consistency)
findings.text:
Phrase: emergency fund "3–6 months of essential expenses"; health "that cap ... is the number your cash reserves should be able to cover."
Why: The two sections give two reserve rules that never meet. For a family on an HDHP, the family out-of-pocket maximum can exceed the starter fund and a large part of 3 months of expenses.
Addition (emergency-fund): "If your health plan has a high deductible or out-of-pocket maximum, make sure the fund, or an HSA balance, can cover it on top of living costs."

findings.head: pr:disability — MED
findings.text:
Phrase: "Group long-term disability commonly replaces about 60% of base salary"
Why: Group plans cap the monthly benefit and usually exclude bonus and commission, so higher earners and variable earners often get well under 60%. Group coverage ends with the job, and the self-employed have none.
Addition: "Group plans usually cap the monthly benefit and ignore bonuses and commissions, and coverage ends when you leave the job; an individual policy fills those gaps."

findings.head: pr:term-life — MED
findings.text:
Phrase: "with no dependents it is rarely needed"; "10–12 times annual income"
Why: Exceptions: co-signed private loans, a business partner, and a spouse who depends on your income even without children. The multiple ignores existing assets and employer group coverage, which is not portable.
Addition: "Subtract savings and existing coverage from the need, and don't rely on employer group life alone, since it usually ends with the job."

findings.head: pr:auto — MED (missing)
findings.text:
Missing: uninsured/underinsured motorist coverage. It protects you from the many drivers carrying only state minimums, and an umbrella usually does not cover it unless added.
Addition: "Carry uninsured/underinsured motorist coverage at the same limits as your liability, since many drivers carry only the state minimum."

findings.head: pr:umbrella — MED
findings.text:
Phrase: "Once net worth or income makes you a lawsuit target, roughly match coverage to net worth."
Why: Risk factors (teen drivers, a pool or trampoline, dogs, rental property, board service) matter as much as net worth. Future wages can be garnished, so a young high earner with little net worth is still exposed.
Addition: "Teen drivers, pools, dogs, rental property and volunteer board seats raise the risk regardless of net worth, and future wages can be collected in a judgment."

findings.head: pr:estate — MED (missing)
findings.text:
Missing: payable-on-death and transfer-on-death registrations on bank and brokerage accounts. These are named in the annual review item but not here. Also missing: power of attorney, healthcare directive and HIPAA authorization for adult children turning 18. Parents lose access then, a classic gap.
Addition: "Payable- or transfer-on-death registrations on bank and brokerage accounts work like beneficiary forms. A child who turns 18 needs their own power of attorney, directive and HIPAA authorization for parents to help in an emergency."

findings.head: pr:identity — MED (missing)
findings.text:
Missing: the IRS Identity Protection PIN, a free protection against tax-return fraud. Planners pair it with the credit freeze.
Addition: "An IRS Identity Protection PIN, free at IRS.gov, stops someone else from filing a tax return in your name; freezes can also be placed for children."

findings.head: pr:identity plain — LOW
findings.text:
Phrase: "telling your bank about money taken without permission"
Why: The original's "electronic transfers" is what the quick-report liability limit covers; checks and other channels have different rules.
Rewrite: "telling your bank quickly about electronic transfers you didn't make limits how much you can lose."

pr:emergency-fund.title: Emergency fund sizing
pr:emergency-fund.body: The conventional target is three to six months of essential expenses — not of income — held in an insured, liquid account. Start with a starter fund of $1,000 or one month of expenses so a small surprise does not become new debt, then build to the full target after the employer match and high-interest debt. Size toward the high end, or beyond it, when income is variable, when one earner supports the household, when there are dependents, or when re-employment in your field is slow.
pr:emergency-fund.plain: The usual target is three to six months of essential costs — not of income — kept in an insured account you can reach quickly. Start with a small fund of $1,000 or one month of costs, so a small surprise doesn't become new debt. Then build to the full target after getting your employer match and paying off high-interest debt. Aim higher, or beyond the range, if your income goes up and down, if one person supports the household, if you have dependents, or if finding a new job in your field takes a long time.
props: Target 3–6 months of essential expenses, not income
Held in an insured, liquid account
Starter fund of $1,000 or one month first
Full target after match and high-interest debt
Size higher for variable income, single earner, dependents, slow re-employment

pr:health.title: Health insurance
pr:health.body: Health coverage is a Tier-1 item in the plan for a reason: an uninsured hospital stay is the most common route from a stable budget to unpayable debt. ACA-compliant plans cap in-network out-of-pocket spending each year (2026 cap: {{fig:aca_oop_max_self}} for one person, {{fig:aca_oop_max_family}} for a family); that cap, not the premium, is the number your cash reserves should be able to cover.
pr:health.plain: Health coverage is a Tier-1 (top-priority) step for a reason: a hospital stay without insurance is the most common way a steady budget turns into debt you can't pay. ACA-compliant plans limit what you pay in-network each year (2026 limit: {{fig:aca_oop_max_self}} for one person, {{fig:aca_oop_max_family}} for a family). That limit, not the premium, is the amount your savings should be able to cover.
props: Health coverage is Tier-1 for a reason
An uninsured hospital stay is the most common route to unpayable debt
ACA plans cap annual in-network out-of-pocket
Reserves should cover that cap, not the premium
The cap has a one-person amount and a family amount

pr:disability.title: Disability insurance
pr:disability.body: For a working adult, disability is more likely than early death, and an earner's future income is usually their largest asset. Group long-term disability commonly replaces about 60% of base salary; if your employer pays the premium, the benefit is taxable, which lowers the real replacement rate. The policy features that decide whether a claim pays — own-occupation versus any-occupation definition, the elimination period, the benefit period — matter as much as the percentage.
pr:disability.plain: For someone who works, becoming disabled is more likely than dying early, and your future pay is usually your biggest asset. Group long-term disability insurance often replaces about 60% of base pay. If your employer pays the premium, the benefit is taxed, so you really get less. The policy details that decide whether a claim pays — whether "disabled" means unable to do your own job or any job, how long you wait before benefits start, how long benefits last — matter as much as the percentage.
props: Disability is more likely than early death for working adults
Future income is usually the largest asset
Group LTD commonly replaces ~60% of base salary
Employer-paid premium → taxable benefit → lower real replacement
Own-occ vs any-occ, elimination period, benefit period matter as much

pr:term-life.title: Term life insurance
pr:term-life.body: Life insurance replaces income for people who depend on it; with no dependents it is rarely needed. The common heuristic for a primary earner with dependents is 10–12 times annual income; the DIME method (debt + income for the years needed + mortgage + education) gives a household-specific number. Term coverage is the default for this job; whole-life policies bundle insurance with a low-return savings component.
pr:term-life.plain: Life insurance replaces income for people who rely on it. If no one depends on you, you rarely need it. A common rule of thumb for a main earner with dependents is 10–12 times yearly income; the DIME method (debt + income for the years needed + mortgage + education) gives a number for your household. Term insurance is the standard choice for this job. Whole-life policies bundle insurance with a savings part that earns little.
props: Life insurance replaces income for dependents
Without dependents it is rarely needed
Heuristic 10–12× income for a primary earner with dependents
Term is the default; whole life bundles a low-return savings part

pr:property.title: Renters or homeowners insurance
pr:property.body: A landlord's policy covers the building, not the tenant's belongings or the tenant's liability; renters insurance covers both. Homeowners should insure to the cost of rebuilding rather than market value, and should know that standard policies exclude flood damage.
pr:property.plain: A landlord's policy covers the building, not a renter's belongings or a renter's liability. Renters insurance covers both. Homeowners should insure for what it would cost to rebuild, not what the home would sell for, and should know that standard policies don't cover flood.
props: Landlord's policy does not cover tenant property or liability
Insure to rebuild cost, not market value

pr:auto.title: Auto insurance
pr:auto.body: State minimum liability limits are set low and can leave your savings exposed after a serious accident. Consumer guidance commonly suggests at least $100,000 per person, $300,000 per accident and $100,000 property damage; umbrella carriers usually require higher underlying limits before they will write a policy.
pr:auto.plain: The minimum liability coverage states require is low, and it can leave your savings at risk after a bad accident. Consumer guides often suggest at least $100,000 per person, $300,000 per accident and $100,000 for property damage. Umbrella insurers usually require higher limits underneath before they will sell you a policy.
props: State minimum liability limits are low and can expose savings
Umbrella carriers require higher underlying limits

pr:umbrella.title: Umbrella liability
pr:umbrella.body: An umbrella policy adds liability coverage on top of auto and homeowners policies. It is inexpensive per dollar of coverage — industry pricing surveys put $1 million at roughly $200–400 a year — and is commonly sized to at least your net worth.
pr:umbrella.plain: An umbrella policy adds liability coverage on top of your auto and home policies. It costs little for the coverage you get — industry price surveys put $1 million at roughly $200–400 a year — and people often buy at least as much as their net worth.
props: Umbrella adds liability on top of auto and homeowners
on top of your auto and home
Commonly sized to at least net worth
at least as much as their net worth

pr:estate.title: Beneficiaries, will, power of attorney, healthcare directive
pr:estate.body: Beneficiary designations on retirement accounts and life insurance pass those assets directly and generally override a will, so they are the first thing to check. A will directs everything else and is where parents name a guardian for minor children; without one, state intestacy law decides. A durable financial power of attorney lets someone you choose manage your finances if you cannot; without one, a family may need a court-appointed guardian or conservator. A healthcare directive (living will plus a healthcare proxy) records your medical wishes and who decides, and a HIPAA authorization lets named people get your medical information. Each is governed by state law.
pr:estate.plain: Beneficiary forms on retirement accounts and life insurance send that money straight to the people named, and they usually win over a will — so check them first. A will covers everything else, and it is where parents name a guardian for young children; without one, your state's law decides who gets what. A durable financial power of attorney lets a person you choose handle your money if you can't; without one, your family may need a court to appoint someone. A healthcare directive (a living will plus a healthcare proxy) records the care you want and who decides for you, and a HIPAA authorization lets people you name get your medical information. State law governs each of these.

A will directs everything else and names a guardian for minors
Without a will, state intestacy law decides
Durable POA lets a chosen person manage finances on incapacity
Without one, a court-appointed guardian/conservator may be needed
Healthcare directive = living will + proxy: wishes and decision-maker
living will plus a healthcare proxy

pr:identity.title: Credit freeze and fraud recovery
pr:identity.body: A security freeze stops new credit being opened in your name and is free by federal law at Equifax, Experian and TransUnion; it does not affect your credit score, and you can lift it temporarily when you apply for credit. You can pull your own reports free every week at AnnualCreditReport.com. If fraud happens, IdentityTheft.gov builds the recovery plan, and reporting unauthorized electronic transfers to your bank quickly limits your liability.

links.label: Annual review · credit freeze and report pull

pr:identity.plain: A security freeze stops anyone from opening new credit in your name. It's free by federal law at Equifax, Experian and TransUnion, it doesn't change your credit score, and you can lift it for a while when you apply for credit. You can check your own credit reports for free every week at AnnualCreditReport.com. If fraud happens, IdentityTheft.gov makes a recovery plan for you, and telling your bank about money taken without permission quickly limits how much you can lose.

stops anyone from opening new credit
Free by federal law at all three bureaus
Can be lifted temporarily to apply
Prompt reporting of unauthorized transfers limits liability
